name: pdk-glom-etl
instr:
Our vendor's order export is now JSON Lines, and we reshape it with `python -m glom` and our existing specs. A few days of the vendor's files are in /data/exports/, and they have to go through as they come.

Please add `jsonl` as a target format. Each nonblank line is its own JSON document, and the spec runs on each one with the usual glom behavior. Print one result per line, in input order, with no surrounding array. Blank and whitespace-only lines print nothing. The other targets keep their whole-document behavior, and the `json` target has to read the vendor's daily summary files. Files and standard input both have to work.

We also pipe the live export in (`tail -f orders.jsonl | python -m glom --target-format jsonl id | head -3`). Each result has to be printed as soon as its line arrives, and once whatever reads the output stops, the command should end quietly with nothing on stderr. With `--scalar`, each output line should be exactly what the `json` target prints for that document alone, and `--indent` never splits a result over several lines.

If a line is bad (malformed JSON, text that can't be decoded, or the spec fails on it), the earlier lines' results should still be printed. Then the command stops with a nonzero exit status and an error on stderr naming the line, like `line 12`, counted the way `sed -n 12p` counts.

There's no network here, and everything is installed in /app.
